slides.title: How the pieces connect
slides.html:
Overview

How the pieces connect

  • React runs in the browser (port 5173)
  • Express runs on the server (port 5000)
  • They talk with fetch and JSON
  • The token proves who is calling

The flow

React (5173)                Express (5000)        MongoDB
LoginForm  --POST /auth/login-->  check password
            <---- { token } ------
JobList    --GET /jobs ---------> Job.find()  ---> jobs
            <---- [ ...jobs ] ----
NewJob     --POST /jobs + token-> protect, create

slides.title: A reusable API helper
slides.html:
Helper

A reusable API helper

  • One place for the base URL
  • Adds the token automatically
  • Throws on errors so you can catch them

src/lib/api.js

const API = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL;
 
export async function api(path, options = {}) {
  const token = localStorage.getItem("token");
  const res = await fetch(API + path, {
    ...options,
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...(token && { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }) },
    body: options.body && JSON.stringify(options.body),
  });
  const data = await res.json().catch(() => null);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data?.message || "Request failed");
  return data;
}

slides.title: Login state with Context
slides.html:
Auth

Login state with Context

  • createContext + a provider at the top
  • Store the user and token in one place
  • Any component can read useAuth()
  • Log out clears both

src/context/AuthContext.jsx

export function AuthProvider({ children }) {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null);
 
  const login = async (email, password) => {
    const data = await api("/auth/login", { method: "POST", body: { email, password } });
    localStorage.setItem("token", data.token);
    setUser(data.user);
  };
  const logout = () => { localStorage.removeItem("token"); setUser(null); };
 
  return <AuthContext.Provider value={{ user, login, logout }}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>;
}

slides.title: Protected pages
slides.html:
Routes

Protected pages

  • Not logged in? Send them to /login
  • Wrap pages that need a user
  • The backend still checks too

App.jsx

function RequireAuth({ children }) {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  if (!user) return <Navigate to="/login" replace />;
  return children;
}
 
<Route path="/jobs/new" element={
  <RequireAuth><NewJob /></RequireAuth>
} />

slides.title: Loading and error states
slides.html:
UX

Loading and error states

  • Show a spinner while waiting
  • Show the server's message on errors
  • Disable buttons while submitting

NewJob.jsx

const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
const [error, setError] = useState("");
 
const submit = async (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  setLoading(true); setError("");
  try {
    await api("/jobs", { method: "POST", body: form });
    navigate("/");
  } catch (err) { setError(err.message); }
  finally { setLoading(false); }
};

slides.title: Adding an AI feature
slides.html:
AI

Adding an AI feature

  • React calls your API
  • Your API calls the AI provider
  • The key never leaves the server

controllers/ai.js

// backend: POST /api/ai/job-description
export const describeJob = async (req, res) => {
  const { title, company } = req.body; const r = await fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: AI_HEADERS, // key + version, built from process.env
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: process.env.AI_MODEL, max_tokens: 400,
      messages: [{ role: "user",
        content: `Write a short job description for a ${title} at ${company}.` }] }),
  });
  const data = await r.json(); res.json({ text: data.content?.[0]?.text || "" });
};

slides.title: Using AI safely in your app
slides.html:
Safety

Using AI safely in your app

Keys on the server

Never put an AI key in React or VITE_ variables.

process.env.AI_API_KEY

Limit usage

Only logged-in users, with a rate limit, so nobody drains your credit.

protect + rateLimit

Check the output

AI can be wrong. Let users edit it before saving.

editable textarea

slides.title: The "Write with AI" button
slides.html:
Build

The "Write with AI" button

  • Calls your backend, not the AI directly
  • Fills the textarea so the user can edit
  • Shows loading while it works

NewJob.jsx

const writeWithAI = async () => {
  setAiLoading(true);
  try {
    const { text } = await api("/ai/job-description", {
      method: "POST",
      body: { title: form.title, company: form.company },
    });
    setForm({ ...form, description: text });
  } catch (err) {
    setError(err.message);
  } finally {
    setAiLoading(false);
  }
};
